submission.justification: Sensor-T2 has the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um) but was only 82.0% efficient after 2e16 neq/cm^2, well below the >=97% end-of-life requirement for the innermost layer, so it does not meet the radiation constraint. Of the two technologies that pass (T1 98.5%, T3 99.2%), T1 resolves better (9.0 um vs 14.0 um at 150 um). So T1 is recommended. Caveats: (1) No simulation tool was available in this session, so I could not scan thickness. 150 um is chosen because it is the only thickness with resolution data (2025 summary), and it is inside the 50-300 um range. The best thickness was not optimised. (2) The resolution numbers are for unirradiated sensors. Resolution after irradiation was not measured. (3) The documents do not say what thickness the test-beam sensors had, so the 98.5% efficiency may not apply exactly at 150 um. Before finalising, run a thickness scan that includes irradiated sensors. Thinner T1 sensors may improve radiation tolerance, but they produce less charge.
